A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StarVector, SVG-Stack, and SVG-Bench. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, equations, and rendered figures, support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v2 limit some implementation conclusions but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-to-SVG experiments and comparisons across SVG-Bench, plus encoder, augmentation, pretraining, and decoding ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original image-to-SVG, text-to-SVG, diagram, and human-evaluation results, including experiments with 1B and 8B models. Some text-generation baseline scores are explicitly borrowed from prior work, but StarVector's results are original.

M1.justification: v1 proposes image-conditioned generation with CLIP and StarCoder-1B. v2 adds text-conditioned fine-tuning and generation, an 8B variant using SigLip and StarCoder2-7B with a 16k context, and inference procedures that bias termination and rank multiple generated candidates. These substantially extend the model and generation procedure.

E1.justification: The four original datasets and their simplified variants remain. v2 adds text-to-SVG training and evaluation using captioned SVG-Stack and SVG-FIGR. It also introduces a focused 472-example SVG-Diagrams test subset selected from SVG-Stack; diagrams already occurred within v1's broader SVG-Stack coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained VTracer, Im2Vec, DeepSVG, and GPT-4 Vision comparisons, v2 evaluates AutoTrace, Potrace, LIVE, and DiffVG in image-vectorization experiments. Its new text-generation comparison includes GPT-4 and CodeLlama, alongside published IconShop, DeepSVG+GAN, and BERT results on SVG-FIGR (Table 4).

E3.justification: v2's main training recipe changes the learning rate from 5e-4 to 1e-5 and the 1B effective batch size from 64 to 128, adds the larger model's settings, and specifies best-of-five inference. Evaluation adds DinoScore, token counts, text-generation metrics, and randomized, anonymized human comparisons. Appendix 11.2 also retains v1's training recipe, leaving assignment of settings to some results unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 retains earlier augmentation, pretraining, decoding, and encoder analyses, although its quantitative encoder table drops SVG-Icons and SVG-Stack. New analyses examine path-count versus quality and runtime, primitive recognition and tag distributions, human alignment of metrics, text-generation temperature sensitivity and failures, and one-versus-five-candidate sampling (Table 3; Appendix 10; Section 11.3).

E5.justification: v2 introduces Spearman correlation analysis relating automatic metrics to human judgments (Section 6.1 and Appendix 10.5). Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new statistical estimation is therefore limited; generating five inference candidates does not establish repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many scores are replaced and substantial results are added. For SVG-Stack, v1 Table 4 reports StarVector MSE/LPIPS of 0.072/0.153; v2 Table 1 reports 0.078/0.149 for 1B and 0.026/0.058 for 8B under revised settings, so these are not controlled version-to-version gains. v2 also adds text, diagram, human-preference, runtime, and token-count results. Many earlier ablation values remain, while their tabulated Chamfer-distance entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a mathematical characterization of DinoScore as L2 distance between DINOv2 features (Section 5.1). Its adapter equations and autoregressive factorization largely formalize or restate material already present in v1 Section 3 and Appendix 10. No new theorems or proofs appear; the distance description is not reconciled with the higher-is-better reporting.

C1.justification: The image-to-code contribution remains, but v2 expands the central claims to text-driven generation and a ten-dataset, three-task benchmark. Its abstract, contributions, and conclusion elevate compactness, semantic primitive recognition, and human-aligned evaluation to central contributions. Text generation changes from a future application in v1 to a demonstrated capability.

C2.justification: v2 extends v1's background-pixel criticism of MSE with explanations involving spatial misalignment, corner artifacts, and human preference for semantic fidelity. It develops primitive usage as an explanation for compactness and discusses speed tradeoffs, caption-quality and compositional failures, and the remaining 16k-context limitation. These substantially expand interpretation and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds captioning prompts and filtering thresholds, font and diagram curation instructions, distributed-training configurations, precision and memory settings, and detailed inference parameters. However, Appendix 11 retains conflicting legacy training and CLIP-encoder descriptions. v1's explicit project code/model repository link is absent from v2; this establishes removed access information, not repository unavailability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially redirects positioning toward primitive-aware multimodal generation and SVG-specific benchmarking. Section 2 adds a datasets-and-benchmarks discussion citing SVGEditBench and VGBench, and incorporates newer foundations including StarCoder2, DINOv2, and SigLip. Earlier GUI/screenshot-to-code and markup-generation discussions and citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusions are extensively rewritten. SVG-Stack receives a standalone section before the method, related work is reorganized, and much baseline and ablation material moves into a substantially restructured appendix. Some legacy passages remain, including duplicated human-evaluation discussion.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview and architecture diagrams and combines v1's full and simplified result tables into a larger display with new metrics and colored token counts. It adds human-preference charts, primitive-code comparisons, tag distributions, and text-generation galleries. Several earlier galleries and the temperature plot are retained or relocated rather than newly generated analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind visual-quality claims: competitive vectorization baselines, primitive and efficiency analyses, and 1,948 judgments from 30 participants address v1's narrower comparisons and reliance on automatic metrics and illustrative examples. Text and diagram evaluations also substantiate expanded applications. Conflicting training/encoder descriptions and the unclear DinoScore distance convention weaken reproducibility and precision, but the broader comparisons and direct human validation provide a substantial net improvement.
